title: GridDyn, HELICS, SCADA, and Local AI Operator Interface

scope.included: User-visible project requests, troubleshooting exchanges, implementation decisions, current deliverables, and handoff information from this conversation.
scope.excluded: System and developer instructions, hidden reasoning, raw tool-call internals, credentials, and unrelated conversations.
scope.assistant_message_fidelity: Assistant entries are concise outcome summaries where the exact prior response was not available as a user-visible transcript.

conversation_summary: The conversation developed a local, advisory-only GridDyn/HELICS/SCADA interface. The system normalizes RTU and SCADA data, applies a deterministic ontology and IEEE reference layer, optionally uses a local Ollama agent, validates evidence before human review, presents a three-column operator dashboard, and adds a separate scientific-literature retrieval check for hallucination prevention. The final software bundle contains the v7 executable and current source packages.

messages.content: GridDyn used in conjunction with Agent LLMs to provide accurate and updated recommendations for Utilities in the event of grid overload or failure. This predictive model will be able to determine failure rate and possible degradation of Utility before disaster strikes. Resource distribution and recommendations will be given to control engineers who can therefore act accordingly to manage any grid where applied. Using HELICs I want to design an interfacing solution that takes crucial information, gathers it into a readable format for backup analysis that can be read by people, make accurate suggestions given what is present and currently ongoing, and make sure to double check to avoid hallucinations
Create me an interface between griddyn and my computer
Create an interface between an AI Agent and HELICS for Griddyn that an AI Agent can read and understand

Create output interface from AI Agent into person readable information, the output should be checked prior to human interaction to check for AI hallucination. The output interface should be interactive. The person should be able to inform the AI agent if there are still issues to go back and recheck for errors. The AI agent should be able to present possible solutions for what is received from the GridDyn interface.
Which AI agents can run locally without internet?
can you write me an install file that does what you just mentioned?
list all python dependencies and create a download program for them

create a training data set based off of real life examples of Asset failure hazard

1. Thermal-aging degradation
2. Protection-trip probability
3. Loss-of-load risk
4. Time-to-limit prediction

build me a compiler that will launch all of the necessary tools and create a basic UI using command line that is navigable an lets me input my desired values. Build an example as well that can be run to demonstrate the software. The UI should show the output below the inputs in a clear manner
can you compile these into an .exe format that I can run

The executable troubleshooting established the distinction between PowerShell commands and Command Prompt, corrected executable location issues, and added explicit CLI/dashboard launch paths.

In a real life systems we would use SCADA as the input for values we are measuring. I have attached a crude drawing of what a possible system using GridDyn could tie into SCADA. RTU's give the information which we want to pull from. There isn't an ontology in place yet for managing if there are possible detected failures or if the grid is strained. Build an ontology based on real world examples that aid and assist real grids. I.E. SDG&E turns off sections of the grid due to high winds -> prevents wild fires.
In this ontology can you include IEEE standards as well

The ontology layer was expanded to normalize SCADA/RTU observations, asset metadata, quality states, hazards, risks, evidence, read-only GridDyn study requests, and approval-required options. An IEEE reference catalog was added for DNP3, protection functions, synchrophasors, time synchronization, COMTRADE, DER/IBR interconnection, cybersecurity, power quality, reliability, and protection references. Standards classify evidence and interfaces; they do not authorize controls or supply utility-specific thresholds.

Can you design a user friendly UI separate from the software that acts as an interface to the package. This should launch at the same time when you run the .exe file. Visually it should not be cluttered. On the left side show all inputs and data. In the middle show what the LLM interprets as possible issues. On the right show the possible solutions as outputs and list them most effective to least effective.

A separate three-column localhost dashboard was added and made the default executable launch path. The left column shows inputs and telemetry, the middle column shows evidence-gated interpretation and recheck feedback, and the right column shows ranked approval-required options. The dashboard is advisory-only and has no grid-control endpoint.

Can you now create an additional check method. Pull every known and recorded scientific paper regarding utilities ever written that has been peer reviewed and approved, compile all of them together and use it as pretraining data for the LLM. Clarify that this is for an additional check against the anti-hallucination. The papers found must include mathematical models that prove something relevant to Utilities. Do not include theory papers.

An independent scientific-evidence gate was added. It uses a curated retrieval manifest rather than claiming exhaustive coverage or silently pretraining on unrestricted copyrighted papers. The gate selects applied papers with mathematical models and validation or case-study evidence, excludes theory-only/review/unverified records, shows DOI/model/validation/limitations in the dashboard, and rejects scientific paper IDs that were not retrieved for the current packet.
can you now compile every file in this chat into one zipped folder
Can you compile every relevant, currently
The incomplete clarification was identified and the scope was narrowed to the latest currently used files rather than every historical version.
all currently used files into one zipped folder

The current-files bundle was assembled from the v7 executable, v7 full source/package archive, dashboard v2 bundle, and SCADA/IEEE ontology v2 bundle. Obsolete v1-v6 executables and superseded bundles were excluded.

technical_decisions.details: The system does not issue breaker operations, dispatch commands, setpoints, automatic PSPS actions, or other grid-control commands. Candidate options require human approval and independent GridDyn/constraint validation.

SCADA/RTU evidence IDs, quality states, timestamps, policy version, unknowns, and limitations remain attached to interpretations and candidate options. Invalid or unsupported LLM output falls back to deterministic screening.
Ollama is optional and local. The deterministic ontology, dashboard, scientific manifest, and safety gate remain usable without Internet access or a running local model.

technical_decisions.decision: Scientific literature is an additional check, not hidden pretraining
technical_decisions.details: The scientific-evidence layer retrieves provenance-preserving paper metadata, mathematical model summaries, validation basis, and limitations. It does not claim that a paper's parameters apply to a live utility asset.
Inputs and data appear on the left, possible issues and evidence checks appear in the middle, and ranked approval-required solutions appear on the right.
